fields.summary: User can reset their password via an emailed link
fields.description:
As a registered user I want to reset my password through a link sent to my email so that I can regain access when I forget it.

Project Key: SMOKE
Issue ID (numeric): 10001

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form sends an email with a single-use password-reset link that is valid for 60 minutes.
2. Opening a reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent shows the message 'This reset link has expired' and a 'Request a new link' button.

attachments.reset-policy.md:
Password reset policy
- A reset link stays valid for 60 minutes.
- At most 3 reset requests per account per hour.

review_comments:
**Review Feedback from Testing Team**

1. Incorporate Rate Limiting from reset-policy.md:
   - According to 'reset-policy.md', there is a limit of at most 3 reset requests per account per hour. Define acceptance criteria for this limit, including expected UI/API behavior and error messaging when a user submits a 4th request within the 60-minute window.

2. Specify Behavior for Non-Registered Emails (User Enumeration Prevention):
   - AC 1 currently only specifies behavior for registered email addresses. Define what occurs when an unregistered or invalid email address is submitted (e.g., display a generic message to prevent account enumeration).

3. Define Locale Handling Based on reset-request.json:
   - The payload in 'reset-request.json' includes a "locale" parameter ("en-GB"). Specify acceptance criteria detailing how locale is passed, whether the email content/template and reset pages must be localized accordingly, and fallback behavior if locale is omitted or unsupported.

4. Clarify Link Invalidation and Reuse Behavior:
   - While AC 1 states the link is single-use, specify the exact message and behavior when a user opens an already-used reset link.
   - Clarify whether requesting a new reset link invalidates previously issued, unexpired links.

5. Add Acceptance Criteria for the Actual Password Reset Flow:
   - The current criteria only cover sending the email and viewing an expired link. Add criteria defining:
     - Form fields and UI displayed upon opening an active/valid link (e.g., 'New Password' and 'Confirm Password').
     - Password validation rules and complexity requirements.
     - Confirmation feedback and navigation/redirection after a successful password update.
     - Invalidation of existing active user sessions upon successful password reset.

6. Detail Submission Feedback and Expired Link Navigation:
   - Specify the immediate UI confirmation message shown on the 'Forgot password' page upon submitting the form.
   - Clarify the action/navigation destination for the 'Request a new link' button in AC 2 (e.g., redirect to the 'Forgot password' form).

test_cases.name: Password reset link generation and single-use validity within 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify requesting a password reset sends a single-use link valid within 60 minutes, resetting the password succeeds, and reusing the link is rejected.
test_cases.precondition: A registered user account exists with email 'user@example.com' and the 'Forgot password' form is open.
test_cases.review_comments:
• Preconditions - Missing mailbox access: Add a precondition stating that the tester has access to the email inbox (or email testing service/inbox mock) for the registered user account. Without this, Step 2 ('Open the password reset link from the received email') cannot be executed step-by-step.
  • Preconditions - Test data duplication: Remove the hardcoded email address ('user@example.com') from the preconditions ('A registered user account exists with email 'user@example.com'...'). Preconditions must not duplicate test step data; rephrase to state that a registered user account exists corresponding to the test data.
  • Step 1 - Expected results clarity: Specify the exact UI state change resulting from form submission on the 'Forgot password' page (e.g., displaying a confirmation message that the password reset link has been sent), rather than vaguely stating 'The form submission is accepted'.
  • Step 1 - Premature assertion in expected results: Remove the assertion that the email contains a 'single-use reset link' from Step 1 expected results. At the point of email receipt, the link's single-use nature cannot be observed or verified; it should simply expect a password reset link, with single-use invalidation verified upon subsequent use.
  • Step 2 & Step 4 - Flawed elapsed time for single-use verification: In Step 2, change 'elapsed time: 60 minutes' to a duration safely within the validity window (e.g., 'elapsed time: 5 minutes' or 'elapsed time: 10 minutes'). Because 60 minutes is the upper boundary of validity, performing Step 2 at 60 minutes causes Step 3 (form submission) and Step 4 (link reuse) to occur after > 60 minutes have elapsed. Consequently, Step 4 cannot definitively verify single-use rejection versus link expiration per AC 2 ('This reset link has expired').
  • Coverage Gap - Rate limiting policy ('reset-policy.md'): The attached reset policy specifies that 'At most 3 reset requests per account per hour' are permitted. Neither SMOKE-T1 nor SMOKE-T2 covers this constraint. Create a dedicated test case to verify that submitting more than 3 reset requests within an hour is throttled/rejected.
  • Coverage Gap - Locale handling ('reset-request.json'): The attachment 'reset-request.json' specifies a locale attribute ('locale: en-GB'). If localized reset emails or reset pages are in scope, update the test case to specify and verify the expected locale/language of the email and reset page.
  • Coverage Gap - Negative scenarios: AC 1 specifies submitting a registered email address. Recommend adding test coverage for negative scenarios on the 'Forgot password' form, such as entering an unregistered email address or an invalid email format.
  • Metadata - Test labels: Populate the 'labels' field with relevant identifiers (e.g., 'smoke', 'password-reset', 'authentication') to ensure test traceability and facilitate test suite filtering.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

steps.description: Enter the registered email address into the email field on the 'Forgot password' form and submit the form.
steps.expected_result: The form submission is accepted, and a password reset email containing a single-use reset link is sent to the registered email address provided in the current step.

steps.description: Open the password reset link from the received email in a web browser within the specified elapsed time.
steps.expected_result: The password reset page is successfully displayed with input fields to set a new password.

steps.description: Enter the new password and confirmation password into the corresponding fields on the password reset page and submit the form.
steps.expected_result: A confirmation message is displayed indicating that the password has been reset successfully.

steps.description: Open the same password reset link used in the previous steps again in the web browser.
steps.expected_result: The password reset page is not displayed, and an error message is shown indicating that the link is invalid or has already been used.

test_cases.name: Expired password reset link handling after 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify that accessing a password reset link more than 60 minutes after generation displays an expiration message and a 'Request a new link' button.
test_cases.precondition: A password reset email containing a reset link has been generated and sent to the user's email address more than 60 minutes ago.
test_cases.review_comments:
• Eliminate duplication between preconditions and test step data: The precondition currently states that the reset email was sent 'more than 60 minutes ago', while Step 1 specifies opening the link 'after the specified elapsed time has passed since it was sent' with test data 'elapsed time: 61 minutes'. Per the quality criteria, test steps must never duplicate preconditions. Remove the '> 60 minutes' condition from the precondition and keep the timing exclusively in the test step's test data (61 minutes) to avoid redundancy and logical conflict.
  • Make preconditions explicit and complete: The precondition vaguely refers to 'the user's email address' without specifying the test account. Specify that a registered user account exists with email 'user@example.com' (as defined in 'reset-request.json' and SMOKE-T1) and that access to the corresponding email inbox/client is available to retrieve the reset link.
  • Add a test step to verify the 'Request a new link' action: Acceptance Criterion 2 specifies that a 'Request a new link' button is displayed. Currently, Step 1 only checks that the button is shown. Add a subsequent test step to click the 'Request a new link' button and verify the resulting application state (e.g. navigation back to the 'Forgot password' form or initiating a new link request).
  • Strengthen Step 1 expected results to ensure security verification: In Step 1 expected results, explicitly verify that the password reset form (new password input fields) is not displayed or accessible, ensuring that an expired token cannot be used to submit a new password.
  • Address Jira issue coverage gap for rate-limiting policy: Attachment 'reset-policy.md' defines a rate limit ('At most 3 reset requests per account per hour'), which is not covered by SMOKE-T2 or the existing test case SMOKE-T1. Recommend creating a dedicated test case to verify that requesting more than 3 reset links within an hour is rejected/throttled.
  • Address locale coverage gap: Attachment 'reset-request.json' specifies locale configuration ('locale': 'en-GB'). Ensure verification that the expiration message 'This reset link has expired' and email notifications are displayed in the expected locale.
  • Align summary terminology with Acceptance Criterion 2: The test summary refers to link 'generation' ('more than 60 minutes after generation'), whereas Acceptance Criterion 2 specifies 'more than 60 minutes after it was sent'. Update the summary wording to 'after it was sent' for consistency with the Jira specification.
  • Populate test case labels: The 'labels' field is currently empty. Add meaningful labels (e.g., 'password-reset', 'authentication', 'boundary-test') to facilitate test filtering, suite organization, and reporting.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

steps.description: Open the password reset link from the received email in a web browser after the specified elapsed time has passed since it was sent.
steps.expected_result: The message 'This reset link has expired' is displayed along with a 'Request a new link' button.

bugs.summary: [Password Reset] - POST /api/password-reset returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
bugs.description:
## Description
An assertion error occurred during the execution of test case SMOKE-T100 ("Password reset email is sent for a registered address"). When sending a POST request to `/api/password-reset` with a registered email address, the server returned an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error instead of the expected HTTP 200, and no password reset email was queued.

Failed Step: Send POST /api/password-reset with a registered email address
Error Message: AssertionError: expected response status 200 but received 500

## Environment Details
- Agent: Smoke API Test Executor (version 9.9-smoke)
- Environment: Smoke Test Environment

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ensure a user account exists for the test email address (precondition: registered@example.com).
2. Send POST /api/password-reset with a registered email address (email=registered@example.com).

## Expected Result
HTTP 200 and a password-reset email is queued.

## Actual Result
HTTP 500 Internal Server Error; no email was queued.
